take_homes: The agent flatters its own work, so a review needs a second reader that doesn't share its history, or me checking it myself.
Plan first, then approve, before the agent writes any files. A blank line stays blank rather than being filled with a plausible guess.
Lessons can be kept in a rules file for the next run. I never saw what that saves in time or money.

monday.move: Ask my controller to try the month-end variance commentary with an agent once. They write the plan first and I check the output against the ledger myself.
monday.stop_condition: The commentary takes longer to correct than to write, or any number can't be traced to the ledger.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: I saw nothing on what it costs per month or per person, and no payback figure. Prework was about my own setup, and the exercise was a personal website. Nothing showed the organisation building a capability, so it still reads as a tool I buy.

one_line: Two useful ideas, that the tool flatters itself and that you plan before you let it write, buried in a personal-website exercise and the same filler paragraph repeated fourteen times, with no cost figure anywhere.
